t: You're at the site of St Swithin, London Stone, which stood on the north side of Cannon Street, between Salters' Hall Court and St Swithin's Lane. The street gets its name from the church. The medieval building was destroyed in the Great Fire, then rebuilt to designs by Sir Christopher Wren, who was given the job of rebuilding 52 City churches. Bombing in the Second World War badly damaged it, and the remains were demolished in 1962. Among those buried here were Sir John Bolles, Sarah Lascelles and Elizabeth Pynsent.
